coverage_failures.evidence_item: Ghidra stageJumpTable (funcdata_block.cc:509-538, confirmed in source): clones a partial Funcdata, calls glb->allacts.setCurrent("jumptable") to switch to the REDUCED 11-group pipeline, runs reset+perform on the clone, then restores the prior action via setCurrent(oldactname).
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: A models this only as feedback edge S3->S2 mechanism_type c (global restart with persisted hints) and collapses it with the multistage-jumptable Override restart. But stageJumpTable is NOT a restart of the same pipeline — it is a recursive sub-decompilation running a DIFFERENT, reduced action set (noproto instead of protorecovery, deadcode+stackptrflow on) on a throwaway clone, returning only the recovered table. A's artifact-invalidation edge model ('this artifact got dirtied') cannot express 'run a different pipeline on a clone and discard it'; there is no artifact of S2 being dirtied — a separate Funcdata is constructed, simplified, and thrown away.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Add a distinct feedback mechanism type 'reduced-pipeline sub-query' (recursive sub-decompilation with an alternate action/group set on a cloned artifact). A must distinguish this from ActionRestartGroup clear-and-replay, which it currently conflates.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: Reko SplitBlock + PromoteBlockWorkItem mutating the procedure graph mid-scan (Scanner.cs:299-415), and Ghidra inlineSubFunction repopulating addrlist/tablelist within one generateOps call (flow.cc:1058-1083).
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: A models the Reko data-pointer/code discovery as feedback edge S1->S3 mechanism_type b (staged re-entry: 'rerun an earlier analysis after later edits to shared state'). That mischaracterizes it: there is NO completed earlier analysis being re-entered — work items are appended to a still-draining priority worklist (procQueue), and blocks are split/promoted while the scan is in progress. It is a growing work-queue over data items (addresses), not a re-run of a stage over a shared artifact.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Add the 'worklist re-enqueue / late-binding' mechanism that B (type f) and C (H1f) both already name. The re-processed unit is an address/work-item, not a stage, and there is no prior stage completion to re-enter.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: Ghidra HighVariable lazy-dirty recompute: merge sets coverdirty/typedirty/symboldirty (variable.hh:120-152) and cover/type/symbol are recomputed on next access, not by re-running a pass (Ghidra report 03 feedback loop 'Merge-Induced Cover Changes').
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: A places merging in S6 and lists 'value identity / merge policy' as a sub-stage but assigns NO feedback mechanism to the demand-driven, object-scoped dirty recompute. A's edge model is strictly 'stage X invalidates artifact of stage Y' (whole-artifact), so an invalidation scoped to a single HighVariable object that is resolved lazily on access has no representation. A simply omits this loop from its feedback_edges list.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Add a 'lazy-dirty recompute' mechanism (demand-driven, object-scoped invalidation) as B (type g) and C (S5->S5) do, and add the corresponding self-edge.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: Reko IAnalysisFactory.CreateSsaAnalyses(stage, ssa, context) injecting arch-specific SSA analyses at AfterRegisterSsa / AfterExpressionCoalescing (report 09); angr OptimizationPassStage 0-11 injection points; Ghidra Architecture extra_pool_rules absorbed into oppool1.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: These are an INJECTION-SLOT axis (where a third party hooks a pass between named boundaries), orthogonal to the artifact-ownership stage axis. A's model has only the stage/sub-stage axis; it forces extra_pool_rules into 'S3 simplification substage' and has no place for the Reko/angr injection-point enums. Both B (critique #4) and C (critique #3) explicitly identify the two-axis structure; A does not, so arch-injection slots are force-placed.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Introduce a second orthogonal axis (injection slot) keyed to inter-stage boundaries, distinct from the artifact-owning stages.

coverage_failures.why_it_fails: B's feedback table models switch recovery as S1->S1 'worklist-re-enqueue (type f)' plus S1->S1 'global restart with persisted hint (H1c)'. Neither captures that Ghidra runs a DIFFERENT reduced action set on a cloned Funcdata. B explicitly enumerates seven mechanism types but still does not include the reduced-pipeline-on-a-clone primitive that C uniquely identifies and that the source confirms.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Add an 8th mechanism (reduced-pipeline sub-query) or fold it into B's roadmap as a first-class kuna capability: B already advocates named reduced pipelines indirectly via 'paramid'/'jumptable' but does not model the recursive clone-and-discard execution.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: angr two-level SSA where SSA-L0 (registers) and SSA-L1 (stack vars) sandwich stack-pointer tracking AND the first callsite construction (clinic.py: TRACK_STACK_POINTERS=4 -> first make-callsites in pre-L1 simplifications -> SSA_LEVEL1).
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: B places SSA in S2 (Definition Web) and Calls in S3, asserting clean named-hook boundaries. But angr's first callsite construction (an S3 concern) runs BETWEEN S2's L0 and L1 sub-artifacts. B acknowledges this in its own critique (S2a/S2b split) but its stage list still presents S2 then S3 as cleanly ordered, so the boundary genuinely straddles two stages on the first pass.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Either split S2 into S2a (register def web) / S2b (stack def web) with an S3-pre wedge, or model the S2/S3 boundary as a first-pass local fixed point rather than a strict order (as C does for S1/S2).

coverage_failures.evidence_item: Ghidra 'Cleanup Pass Timing' decision (report 00): actcleanup is deferred to AFTER fullloop specifically so its rules do not retrigger type-inference/proto changes that would restart mainloop.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: This is a pure SCHEDULING decision (when to run a quiescent pass to guarantee termination), not a decision about an artifact's content. B's decision-centric stages key everything to 'what the decompiler commits to and revises'; cleanup-timing commits to nothing — it is about ordering to avoid a feedback edge. B can only file it under S2's 'value-propagation/simplification quiescence', which misrepresents a termination-policy decision as a simplification-content decision.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Add a scheduling/termination-policy attribute to sub-stages (borrow C's lens) capturing 'deferred to avoid retriggering edge X', rather than treating it as a content decision.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: Pipeline-configuration / scheduler decisions: 'Universal vs Derived Actions', 'Maximum Restart Count (maxrestarts=1)', 'Rule Repeat Strategy', 'Root Action Selection / buildDefaultGroups' (report 00); angr preset selection; Reko priority-queue ordering.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: C's stage list S1-S9 owns concrete artifacts (flow, calls, SSA, simplified IR, vars, types, AST, display, text) but NO stage owns the scheduler/pipeline configuration itself. C discusses the restart driver and named reduced pipelines only in kuna_implications, not as a stage or sub-stage with an intervention surface. So these durable configuration assertions (which select which stages run at all) have no home in C's stage taxonomy, even though C's whole thesis is scheduling-centric.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Add an orthogonal configuration/scheduler plane (analogous to A's and B's S0) that owns pipeline-scope assertions: action-group toggles, restart budget, reduced-pipeline selection, preset choice. C's strength (the scheduler) is paradoxically not a first-class stage.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: First-pass ordering of S1 (Flow & Code Recovery) vs S2 (Call-Interface Recovery): Reko recovers call interfaces bottom-up over SCCs only knowable after scanning; angr recovers calling conventions before AIL conversion for non-pcode arches but after for pcode.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: C asserts stages 'trigger linearly on the first pass' (the user's Stage definition) yet S1<->S2 form a cycle on the first pass that is architecture/tool-conditional. C admits this in critique #6, so by its own analysis the linear-first-pass property is violated at the S1/S2 boundary — a coverage failure against the user's Stage definition.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Represent the S1/S2 relationship as a first-pass local fixed point (mutual dependency) rather than a strict order, and state explicitly that artifact-ownership defines the dependency skeleton while first-pass order is partly nominal.

coverage_failures.evidence_item: Ghidra fuses type inference (ActionInferTypes, 7-pass) and stack restructuring (ActionRestructureVarnode) and value-set/nonzero analysis INSIDE the single mainloop fixed point, while angr/Reko run type inference as a separate post-stabilization solver (Typehoon / union-find) decoupled from variable recovery.
coverage_failures.why_it_fails: Every proposal presents value-facts, type-facts, variables, and (for A) range as temporally separable stages/sub-stages with directed edges between them. For Ghidra these do not materialize as temporally distinct artifacts — they co-evolve to a mutual fixed point in one loop (ActionInferTypes interleaves with ActionConstantPtr, ValueSet-driven ActionDeterminedBranch, and ActionRestructureVarnode). A's S4<->S5/S5<->S6, B's S5->S4, and C's S6->S5 edges all impose a producer/consumer order that Ghidra does not have on the first pass.
coverage_failures.suggested_fix: Mark the (type, variable, value) cluster as a mutual fixed point whose internal scheduling regime is a per-decompiler sub-stage decision (fused-in-mainloop vs separate-terminal-solver), not a fixed inter-stage order — the taxonomy must not bake one decompiler's schedule into the stage order.

forced_placements: A — Image & Symbol Map (S1) as a stage with its own invalidation story is a near-phantom for Ghidra and angr. Ghidra's frontend (flow.cc) assumes the CFG/Funcdata is handed in and only maps globals LATE (ActionMapGlobals, coreaction.cc:5889); angr's loader runs entirely before the decompiler. Only Reko (DataScanner discovering code pointers) and angr's late memory_data writeback materialize an invalidatable image artifact. A's own rule ('a stage exists iff >=2 decompilers materialize a distinguishable artifact with its own invalidation story') is barely met — the invalidation story is essentially Reko-only plus an angr afterthought, echoing the old taxonomy's Loader/Decode phantom split.

A — Decode-error policy, code/data partition, and reachability pruning (removeUnreachableBlocks) are spread thin across A's S1 (partition substage) and S2 (decode-error substage) with no clean owner for reachability pruning, which is a flow decision that follows from determined-branch/PIC/truncation. B gives it an explicit S1 'reachability pruning' substage; A forces it into the gap between S1 and S2/S3.

A — Architecture rule injection (extra_pool_rules) and Reko IAnalysisFactory injection slots are forced into 'S3 algebraic/dead-code simplification' and 'S0 pipeline-scope assertion', conflating a where-to-hook injection-slot axis with stage membership.

B — Lazy-dirty HighVariable recompute is named as mechanism (g) but B's S4 (Variable & Storage Model) treats merging as a content decision; the demand-driven object-scoped recompute is a scheduling property of the artifact, awkwardly attached to a content stage.

C — The S8 (Display Lowering) vs S9 (Emission & Refinement) split is thin: both own near-terminal render concerns and the cast/format/naming decisions could equally live in either. C forces 'cast & operator strategy' into S8 and 'text + map emission' into S9, but Ghidra's ActionSetCasts and PrintC are one continuous emission concern; this is a 2-stage split where 1 would do (mirror of the old taxonomy's C-Lowering/C-Render over-split).

C — Pipeline/scheduler configuration (group toggles, maxrestarts, preset, reduced-pipeline selection) is forced out of the stage list entirely into kuna_implications prose, despite being the central object of a scheduling-centric taxonomy.
cross_proposal_assessment:
"H4 (artifact-keyed stages) is the strongest hypothesis and all three proposals adopt it as the stage skeleton; the evidence vindicates it (Ghidra physically separates bblocks/sblocks/jumpvec/HighVariable/TypeFactory/ScopeLocal; feedback edges are literally artifact invalidations). So the stage SPINE should be shared, not chosen.

The three proposals are strongest in three non-overlapping dimensions, and the right answer grafts each into a single model:

- Proposal A owns the best ARTIFACT insights: (1) SSA is a reversible PROPERTY of the op-graph, not a stage — verified by Reko UnSsaTransform(false) at DataFlowAnalysis.cs:309 and Ghidra heritage adding MULTIEQUAL into the existing Varnode web; this kills the old taxonomy's SSA stage. (2) The assertion store is an ORTHOGONAL PLANE (S0) read by every stage, not a sequential stage-0 — the only honest model of 'edit DB, clearAnalysis, rerun'. (3) Region tree (sblocks) is a distinct artifact from the CFG (bblocks). A's weaknesses: it under-types feedback (only H1's 5 types), so it cannot express stageJumpTable, worklist-promotion, or lazy-dirty; and its S1 image stage is near-phantom for 2 of 3 tools.

- Proposal B owns the best DECISION/INTERVENTION catalog: every sub-stage carries an assertion type AND a LATENT flag (decision the tool makes but does not let you override) that doubles as the kuna product roadmap (S1.switch table, S2.range granularity, S3.maxpass budget, S4.explicit-vs-implied per variable, S5.solver cap, S6.edge virtualization/quality, S7.schema precedence). B also correctly takes the FINER grain (angr's ClinicStage 0-15) for the S2/S3/S4 boundaries and flags that Reko's 4-member AnalysisStage would under-segment. B's weakness: it still folds stageJumpTable into a plain restart and its S2/S3 boundary straddles angr's interleaved L0/callsite/L1.

- Proposal C owns the best FEEDBACK/SCHEDULING model and is the ONLY proposal that correctly captures the source reality of stageJumpTable as a reduced-pipeline sub-query (verified funcdata_block.cc:509-538), the worklist-promotion mechanism, the lazy-dirty recompute, the restart-vs-subquery distinction, the survivability axis (what outlives clearAnalysis/cache), and — most importantly for kuna — re-run SCOPE as a first-class edge attribute (angr reflow re-runs S5+ only; clears_cache=True re-runs S1+; Ghidra always full). C's weakness: no stage owns the scheduler/config it champions, the S8/S9 split is thin, and S1/S2 first-pass order is admittedly violated.

Best single fit: C fits the evidence's defining property (decompilers are schedulers, not feed-forward pipelines) most faithfully, because every feedback loop in all 10 files maps to one of its typed edges WITH a re-run scope, and only C captures the reduced-pipeline sub-query that the source actually performs. Graft onto C: A's SSA-as-property and S0-orthogonal-plane and region/CFG artifact split; B's sub-stage assertion+LATENT catalog and finer (angr-grained) S2/S3/S4 boundaries and explicit injection-slot/admission-policy concepts."
synthesis_recommendation:
"STAGE LIST (artifact-keyed spine, H4; SSA as property per A; region split from AST per all three):
- S0 Assertion/Knowledge plane — ORTHOGONAL, not ordered. Owns durable typed assertions (Ghidra Symbol DB + Override + locks; angr KB + variables_with_manual_types + DecompilationCache; Reko Program.User.*) AND pipeline/scheduler configuration (group toggles, maxrestarts budget, reduced-pipeline/preset selection, admission policy HARD-vs-HINT). Fixes C's gap (scheduler had no home) and A/B's S0.
- S1 Image & Code Partition — bytes + segment/symbol map + code/data/pointer partition + decoder context. Keep, but flag (per A's own rule) that its invalidation story is strong only in Reko; in Ghidra/angr it is mostly read-once.
- S2 Op-Graph & CFG — the central mutable IR (PcodeOp/Varnode web + bblocks + jumptable sub-artifact). SSA is a REVERSIBLE PROPERTY sub-stage here (not a stage), verified by UnSsaTransform. Algebraic/dead-code simplification is the local-fixed-point sub-stage. Adopt B's finer grain: if targeting angr fidelity, expose register-def-web vs stack-def-web as sub-artifacts with the S3-callsite wedge between them.
- S3 Call & Prototype Specs — FuncCallSpecs/prototype/CC; interprocedural SCC model lives here.
- S4 Value & Type Facts — fuse range + type lattice (per A) as ONE co-iterated fact fabric; mark the (type<->variable<->value) cluster as a MUTUAL FIXED POINT whose schedule (Ghidra fused-in-mainloop vs angr/Reko terminal solver) is a sub-stage decision, not an inter-stage order.
- S5 Variable & Storage Model — HighVariable/unified vars/webs; merge, stack-frame carving, explicit-vs-implied.
- S6 Region Hierarchy — distinct artifact (sblocks/GraphRegion); enables the SAILR rollback edge.
- S7 Structured AST — schema matching + goto minimization (quality signal).
- S8 Token Stream & Text — MERGE C's S8+S9 into one (cast/format/naming + emission + LLM-refinement-as-assertion-writer); avoids the thin Display/Emission over-split.

SUB-STAGE CATALOGS TO KEEP: Keep B's full sub-stage list verbatim with its two columns (assertion type + LATENT flag = kuna roadmap), and ADD C's two columns to every sub-stage: (1) minimal-invalidated-artifact / re-run scope, (2) survivability (does the assertion outlive clearAnalysis/cache). Keep A's four assertion classes (Fact, Structural, Identity/Name, Configuration). Add an INJECTION-SLOT axis (orthogonal to stages) for arch hooks: Reko IAnalysisFactory stages, angr OptimizationPassStage 0-11, Ghidra extra_pool_rules — neither a stage nor a sub-stage.

FEEDBACK EDGE MODEL: Use C's typed edges 'stage X dirties artifact of stage Y', each tagged with C's four scheduling properties (quiescence condition, invalidation trigger, rewind scope op/block/region/function/program, surviving durable state). Expand H1 to SEVEN+ mechanism types: (a) local fixed point; (b) staged re-entry; (c) global restart clear-and-replay; (c') reduced-pipeline sub-query [NEW — stageJumpTable, the decisive break that only C captures]; (d) outer KB re-decompile [parameterize by re-run scope: reflow S4+ vs full S1+]; (e) speculate-validate-rollback [model as a per-stage ACCEPT POLICY with a quality metric, not a single SAILR-specific mechanism — Ghidra's double ActionBlockStructure is the weak form, Reko's last-resort-goto is the degenerate accept-anything form]; (f) worklist re-enqueue / late-binding; (g) lazy-dirty recompute. Reframe (b)/(c)/(c')/(d) as a single 'dirty-an-artifact, re-run-its-producers' operation parameterized by RE-RUN SCOPE (the most important refinement for kuna's interactive/LLM loop). Note mutual-exclusion: Ghidra gates restart off during jumptable recovery (isJumptableRecoveryOn) — two mechanisms can be mutually disabling.

KUNA GUIDANCE: Since kuna extracts Ghidra, expose in order: (1) S0 assertion store + scheduler config (already exist as Symbol DB/Override/group toggles); (2) scope-aware re-run replacing blunt clearAnalysis (tag each assertion with its minimal-invalidated artifact, compute the transitive edge closure, re-run only that suffix — angr reflow philosophy); (3) the named reduced pipelines (jumptable/paramid/normalize) as first-class, since stageJumpTable proves switch recovery REQUIRES a reduced sub-pipeline; (4) port SAILR-style accept-policy/quality-rollback (mechanism e) to S6/S7 — the single biggest capability gap vs angr."
